# Notices {#sec-vocab-notices}

[Normative]{.status}

Terms for **notices**: Things an authority issues about an area, or about other Things, for the attention of those who are or may be there.
Examples are a management zone, an exclusion zone around a whale, and a navigational warning.

A notice is not an observation (@sec-vocab-observations).
A sighting records what someone saw; a notice says what an authority advises, requests or requires, and it may refer to what was seen (@sec-sightings-organisms).
The two can travel in the same message, as over AIS, without becoming one another (@sec-binding-ais).

See [provisional decision 0017](https://github.com/NMEA-Cloud/Framework/blob/main/decisions/0017-sightings-organisms-notices.md).

## What a notice holds

::: {.callout-note title="Placeholder"}
The terms, meanings and sources below are candidates and have not been agreed.
:::

| Term | Meaning | Possible source |
|---|---|---|
| Notice | A Thing an authority issues about an area or other Things | *To be decided* |
| Issuer | The authority that issued the notice, by IRI | `prov:wasAttributedTo` [@prov-o] — *to be confirmed* |
| Area | Where the notice applies | Area, in the core vocabulary (@sec-vocab-core) |
| Validity | The period during which the notice applies; its end is a scheduled update (@sec-changes) | Time, in the core vocabulary (@sec-vocab-core); `dcterms:valid` — *to be confirmed* |
| Issued, modified | When the notice was issued, and when it last changed | `dcterms:issued`, `dcterms:modified` — *to be confirmed* |
| Replaces | A notice that this one supersedes | `dcterms:replaces` — *to be confirmed* |
| Subject | What the notice concerns, for example marine mammals in the area, or a restricted area | *To be decided*; see the descriptions of the AIS Area Notice and Geographic Notice ASMs |
| Action | What vessels are asked to do, for example to reduce speed or keep clear | *To be decided* |
| Status | Whether the notice is in force: active or inactive, as for a management area it announces, or withdrawn, cancelled or expired, each set by an update (@sec-changes) | *To be decided* |
| Text | Words for people | *To be decided* |
| Refers to | The Things the notice concerns, such as a management area, an organism, a sighting, or the regulation that applies | A relationship (@sec-relationships) |

: Candidate terms for notices {#tbl-notice-terms}

A notice's terms of use are stated by its issuer, as for any Thing ([NCF-SEM-020](../overview/semantic-model.qmd#ncf-sem-020)).

## The life of a notice

A notice changes over its life as any Thing does (@sec-changes), and each change is made by its issuer:

Creation
: The authority issues the notice.

Update
: The authority revises the notice: its area, its validity, its text, its status or anything else.
  It remains the same notice, with the same identifier ([NCF-SEM-002](../overview/semantic-model.qmd#ncf-sem-002)).
  Withdrawing or cancelling the notice is an update.

Coming into force
: For a notice that applies from a later time, an update scheduled for the start of its validity.
  The notice is created at once, so that the start can be changed.

Expiry
: An update scheduled for the end of its validity.

Both are held within the notice, as its validity, so every revision of the notice restates them, and a revision that changes the validity reschedules them ([NCF-SEM-030](../overview/semantic-model.qmd#ncf-sem-030)).

A binding that cannot carry a notice whole carries these changes instead, as the AIS binding does (@sec-binding-ais).

A notice that is withdrawn or expires is updated, not deleted.
It remains available at its IRI, marked as withdrawn or expired, so that references to it, from other notices, from sightings or from records, do not dangle.

::: {.requirement #ncf-voc-not-001}
**NCF-VOC-NOT-001** · *Draft*\
A notice that is withdrawn or expires SHOULD remain available at its IRI, marked as withdrawn or expired.
:::

The requirement is on the notice's origin (@sec-origins).
A receiver may discard its cached representation of a notice it no longer needs, which is not a change to the notice (@sec-validity).

How a receiver tells which revision of a notice it holds, and whether it is the latest, is not particular to notices (@sec-versions).

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
Which kinds of update does a notice distinguish, such as withdrawn, cancelled and expired, and what does each tell a receiver, for example whether the notice was issued in error?
:::

## Identity of a notice {#sec-notice-identity}

A notice's identifier is the IRI its issuer gives it.
Every participant that holds or relays the notice identifies it by that IRI once it knows it, so that the notice is the same Thing wherever it is held ([NCF-SEM-002](../overview/semantic-model.qmd#ncf-sem-002)).
A receiver's copy of a notice is the notice itself, held as a cached representation (@sec-origins), not a Thing of the receiver's own.
What the receiver knows about its copy, such as when and over which transport it was received and whether it is complete, is the provenance of the copy (@sec-trust-security), not part of the notice.

::: {.requirement #ncf-voc-not-002}
**NCF-VOC-NOT-002** · *Draft*\
A participant that holds or relays a notice MUST identify it by the IRI its issuer gave it, once it knows that IRI.
:::

A transport that cannot carry the IRI identifies a notice by an alias instead, as AIS does (@sec-ais-identity).

## Kinds of notice

Notices of management areas
: A notice that announces a management area (@sec-management-areas), its activation for a period, or a change to it.

Zones around organisms
: A zone around an organism, such as a whale (@sec-sightings-organisms): either a management area that moves with the organism, which a notice says is active or not,
  or a notice with an area of its own (@sec-management-areas).

Navigational warnings
: Warnings of dangers to navigation.
  IHO S-124 specifies navigational warnings for S-100 systems, including NAVAREA, coastal and local warnings, with their areas and cancellations [@iho-s124].

## Management areas {#sec-management-areas}

A **management area** is an area in which official rules apply to vessels, such as limits on speed, for example in a protected area.
It is not a notice but a Thing of its own, with its own IRI, usually defined in regulation and standing for years.
A notice refers to it: to announce it, its activation for a period, or a change to it.
The management area is the same Thing in every notice that refers to it ([NCF-SEM-002](../overview/semantic-model.qmd#ncf-sem-002)).

A management area's area is either fixed or relative:

Fixed
: A shape on the chart, as for a protected area defined in regulation.

Relative
: A rule that places the area relative to another Thing, such as within 1000 m of an organism, so that the area moves with it.
  The rule may be given for a kind of Thing, such as a species, so that it applies around every organism of that species.
  The area at any time follows from the Thing's last known position.

A notice that refers to a relative management area says whether it is active.
For example, an authority may mark a whale's zone inactive when the whale's position has become too uncertain.

Not every zone is a management area.
An authority may also issue a notice that defines an area of its own, for a zone that no standing rule describes.

::: {.callout-note title="Placeholder"}
The terms, meanings and sources below are candidates and have not been agreed.
:::

| Term | Meaning | Possible source |
|---|---|---|
| Management area | An area in which official rules apply to vessels | *To be decided* |
| Responsible authority | The authority responsible for the area, by IRI | *To be decided* |
| Area | Where the rules apply, if the area is fixed | Area, in the core vocabulary (@sec-vocab-core) |
| Relative to | The Thing, or kind of Thing such as a species, that a relative area moves with | A relationship (@sec-relationships) |
| Distance | How far from that Thing a relative area extends | *To be decided* |
| Rules | The regulation that defines the area and what it requires | A relationship (@sec-relationships) |
| Applies to | The vessels the rules apply to, for example by length or speed | *To be decided* |

: Candidate terms for management areas {#tbl-management-area-terms}

See [provisional decision 0017](https://github.com/NMEA-Cloud/Framework/blob/main/decisions/0017-sightings-organisms-notices.md).

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
How are relative areas expressed, beyond a distance from a Thing, given that a geometry cannot express them?
Does a relative area grow with the uncertainty of the Thing's position, or does the notice go inactive instead, and who decides?
Is a rule given for a species one management area, or one for each organism it applies around?
Is a notice's status a property of the notice, or is an inactive zone a withdrawal?
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
How do notices relate to S-124 navigational warnings: is a navigational warning a kind of notice, and can a notice be mapped to and from an S-124 warning without loss?
:::

## Authorities

An authority is a participant that issues notices under its own responsibility, such as a maritime administration or a wildlife management agency.
Like every Thing it is identified by an IRI, and as a data owner it can sign its notices (@sec-data-owners).

Anyone can issue a notice: the framework cannot prevent a participant from publishing or transmitting one, and does not try to.
Whether a receiver acts on a notice depends on its relationship to the issuer, and on its trust in the issuer's identity.
That trust differs by transport (@sec-trust-security):
over IP it rests on the issuer's identity as a data owner (@sec-data-owners), and over VHF on the regulation of who may transmit (@sec-ais-trust).
